target.title: feat(compaction): add identifier survival validation after summarization
target.body:
Fixes #90010
Fixes #79588

## Summary

Improve compaction identifier survival with transcript-wide extraction and quality-guard retry hints. Fixes two security/correctness issues found during review:

**Fix 1 — Sanitize string-encoded JSON arguments before extraction**: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` now parses string-encoded tool arguments as JSON and passes the parsed object through `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before identifier scanning. Previously, string arguments (e.g. OpenAI's JSON-stringified format) were appended raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`.

**Fix 2 — Fail strict compaction when cap recovery cannot fit**: When strict mode detects that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, compaction is now cancelled instead of returning a summary with known identifier loss. This prevents the session from continuing in a state where strict-required identifiers are silently dropped.

## Changed files

- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.ts` — Parse string args as JSON, sanitize via `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before appending; non-JSON strings still pass through
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.ts` — Cancel compaction (return `{ cancel: true }` with reason) when strict cap recovery overflows instead of silently skipping
- `src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts` — Three regression tests: string-encoded JSON credential sanitization, non-JSON passthrough, strict-mode cap overflow cancel

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Two security/correctness issues in compaction identifier survival. (1) `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` appended string-encoded tool arguments raw, allowing credential values like `{"token":"deadbeef12345678"}` to feed the hex identifier extractor and leak into `## Exact identifiers`. (2) When strict mode detected that final capping removed required identifiers and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS`, the summary was returned with known identifier loss instead of cancelling compaction.

Real environment tested: macOS 15.5 arm64, Node v22.19.0, pnpm v11.2.2. Built from source on branch `compaction-identifier-survival-validation` at `/tmp/wt-75336`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

Step 1. Create proof script exercising production `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers`, `extractOpaqueIdentifiers`, `extractIdentifiersFromMessages`, `computeLostIdentifiers`, and `capCompactionSummary`:

```typescript
import {
  extractMessageTextForIdentifiers,
  extractOpaqueIdentifiers,
  extractIdentifiersFromMessages,
  computeLostIdentifiers,
} from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard-quality.js";
import { testing } from "./src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.js";
const { capCompactionSummary, MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS } = testing;
```

Step 2. Validate Fix 1, string-encoded JSON args with credential `token` field:

```typescript
const msg = {
  role: "assistant",
  content: [{
    type: "functionCall", id: "call_1", name: "configure",
    arguments: '{"token":"deadbeef12345678","endpoint":"https://api.acme.io/v2"}',
  }],
};
const text = extractMessageTextForIdentifiers(msg);
assert(!text.includes("deadbeef12345678"));    // credential redacted
assert(text.includes("https://api.acme.io/v2")); // non-credential survives
```

Step 3. Validate Fix 2, capping loses identifiers and recovery overflows:

```typescript
const transcriptIds = extractIdentifiersFromMessages([
  { role: "user", content: "deploy hash a1b2c3d4e5f6" },
]);
const oversized = "## Decisions\nKeep flow.\n## Exact identifiers\n"
  + "x".repeat(MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS) + "\na1b2c3d4e5f6";
const capped = capCompactionSummary(oversized);
const lost = computeLostIdentifiers(transcriptIds, capped);
assert(lost.length > 0);  // identifier at tail truncated by capping
const recovered = `${capped}\n\n## Exact identifiers (recovered)\n- ${lost[0]}`;
assert(recovered.length > MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS); // recovery overflows
```

Step 4. Run `npx tsx proof-75336.ts` from the patched branch.

Evidence after fix:

```console
$ cd /tmp/wt-75336 && npx tsx proof-75336.ts

[Proof 1] String-encoded JSON args sanitization
  PASS credential token value is redacted from string args
  PASS non-credential endpoint survives sanitization
  PASS hex identifier extractor does not capture redacted credential
  PASS non-JSON string args pass through for extraction

[Proof 2] Identifier loss detection after capping
  PASS transcript identifiers extracted from messages
  PASS hex identifier normalized to uppercase
  PASS capped summary respects size limit
  PASS identifier at tail is lost after capping
  PASS recovery block exceeds cap (triggers cancel in strict mode)

Results: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Observed result after fix:

Fix 1: `extractMessageTextForIdentifiers` no longer leaks credential-field values from string-encoded JSON arguments. The `token` field value `deadbeef12345678` is redacted by `sanitizeDiagnosticPayload` before the hex identifier extractor can capture it. Non-credential fields and non-JSON strings pass through normally.

Fix 2: When strict mode detects identifier loss after capping and the recovery block would exceed `MAX_COMPACTION_SUMMARY_CHARS` (16,000 chars), compaction is cancelled with a diagnostic reason instead of returning a summary with known missing identifiers. The cancel reason is stored via `setCompactionSafeguardCancelReason` for downstream diagnostics.

What was not tested: Live compaction with a real model and conversation history (requires a running OpenClaw session with enough context to trigger compaction).

## Rank-up follow-up (2026-07-09)

ClawSweeper P1s:

1. Gate post-cap strict identifier recovery/cancel on `qualityGuardEnabled` so `qualityGuard.enabled: false` keeps the opt-out.
2. Redact credential name/value shapes (`token: deadbeef...`) from non-JSON tool argument strings before identifier extraction.

Terminal confirmation:

```console
$ node ./node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/agents/agent-hooks/compaction-safeguard.test.ts -t "redacts credential name|skips post-cap strict|cancels strict compaction when cap"
 ✓ redacts credential name/value shapes from non-JSON string arguments
 ✓ cancels strict compaction when cap recovery would exceed size limit
 ✓ skips post-cap strict identifier audit when qualityGuard is disabled

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  6 passed (filtered)
```

## What Problem This Solves

Static provider catalog conversion did not preserve all provider/model metadata consistently. The concrete current-main gap is provider-level `params`: static-catalog rows can define provider request params, but the returned runtime model did not merge those provider params with model params.

This PR also makes the static provider catalog converter explicitly carry `compat` and `mediaInput` so the returned runtime model preserves the same schema-valid metadata downstream payload and capability code expects.

## Why This Change Was Made

The runtime should preserve schema-valid provider/model metadata when resolving static provider catalog models. This is a metadata-propagation fix in `modelFromProviderStaticCatalog`; it does not add a new config key, policy path, transport, or custom-provider tool API.

Reviewer scope:
- This PR proves static provider catalog params/metadata propagation into the resolved runtime model and OpenAI-compatible request params.
- The proof is intentionally scoped away from the separate live-session `Tool exec not found` issue, which is not evidence for or against this metadata path.
- Current main already keeps normal configured-provider compat flowing in other paths, and tools are permissive unless `compat.supportsTools === false`; the changed path here is static provider catalog conversion.

## User Impact

Users and bundled/provider catalogs can define provider-level request params and model metadata without losing that metadata during static provider catalog model resolution. Downstream payload generation and capability checks then receive the resolved model shape consistently.

## Evidence

Behavior or issue addressed:
- Static provider catalog conversion merges provider-level and model-level `params`, with model-level values taking precedence.
- Static provider catalog conversion preserves model `compat` metadata.
- Static provider catalog conversion preserves model `mediaInput` metadata.

target.title: fix: skip setup-only channel plugins in outbound resolution and drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect
target.body:
## Summary

When the qqbot WebSocket reconnects after a session timeout (close code `4009`), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returns a setup-only plugin stub that lacks any send capability. This causes the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error, and all messages queued during the disconnection window are permanently lost.

## Root Cause

`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolves the first matching plugin entry for a channel id without verifying that the entry actually has send capability (`outbound.sendText`, `message.send.text`, etc.). During qqbot WebSocket reconnection, a setup-only plugin entry (registered for configuration/pairing but not for message delivery) shadows the real sending plugin, causing the resolution to short-circuit with a non-functional stub.

Regression introduced in 2026.5.28 (commit `e932160`).

## Fix

### 1. Split outbound channel resolution into shared and delivery paths (`channel-resolution.ts`)

Add a `channelPluginCanSend()` predicate that checks for any of the 10 known send methods across both the legacy `outbound` adapter and the newer `message.send` adapter:

- `outbound.sendText / sendMedia / sendPayload / sendPoll / sendFormattedText / sendFormattedMedia`
- `message.send.text / media / payload / poll`

Instead of gating the shared `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` resolver (which would break action-only channel plugins that have `actions.handleAction` but no send capability), a new **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`** resolver applies the send-capability guard exclusively for message delivery paths.

- **`resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`**: Shared resolver — returns any matching plugin regardless of send capability, preserving resolution for action dispatch, target resolution, and other non-send callers.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`**: Delivery resolver — skips setup-only entries and only returns plugins that can actually send messages.
- **`resolveOutboundChannelMessageAdapter()`**: Updated to use the delivery resolver.
- **`message.ts`**: `sendMessage`/`sendPoll` updated to use the delivery resolver.

### 2. Align the direct delivery path with the operation-aware resolver (`deliver.ts`)

The preflight resolver was operation-aware, but the actual direct delivery handler reloaded the adapter capability-blind: `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` → `loadChannelOutboundAdapter` resolved the first registry entry for the channel id (`createChannelRegistryLoader((entry) => entry.plugin.outbound)`) without checking send capability. A setup-only shell with a defined-but-non-send `outbound` (`{ deliveryMode: "direct" }`, no `sendText`) pinned ahead of the runtime sender therefore still shadowed the real adapter on the direct send path, throwing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` even after preflight had selected a valid plugin. This also affected the reconnect drain path, which has no preflight.

`loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now resolves through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight (with `allowBootstrap`, operation `text`), so preflight and the actual direct delivery handler share one send-capability-aware resolution path. The previous manual bootstrap-and-retry is removed because the resolver's `allowBootstrap` performs the equivalent lazy materialize-then-retry. The generic registry loader and the CLI/SDK surfaces are left untouched.

### 3. Drain pending deliveries on qqbot reconnect (`extensions/qqbot/src/channel.ts`)

The `onReady` and `onResumed` gateway callbacks now call `drainPendingDeliveries()` from the plugin SDK delivery queue runtime, recovering messages that were queued while the WebSocket was disconnected. The drain is:

- Filtered by channel (`qqbot`) and account id, with a fallback for default-account entries where `accountId` may be `undefined`
- Deduplicated via `drainKey` to prevent concurrent drains
- Wrapped in try/catch so drain failures do not break the reconnection flow

### 4. Route the gateway poll handler through the operation-aware resolver (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`)

The gateway `poll` handler still resolved its outbound plugin via the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, while `sendPoll` (`message.ts`) and the direct text delivery path (`deliver.ts`) already routed through the operation-aware `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()`. This left the gateway poll endpoint as the last surface where a setup-only / text-only first-match plugin could shadow a poll-capable runtime fallback and force a spurious `"unsupported poll channel"`, even though the new resolver test proves the poll-capable fallback should win.

The poll handler now resolves through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, mirroring the text delivery path. The `durationSeconds` / `isAnonymous` capability checks below the resolution now read from the same poll-capable plugin that serves `sendPoll`, so the capability gate and the actual send no longer disagree. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file (the `send` and `action` surfaces) are intentionally left on the shared resolver, since action-only plugins must still resolve without send capability.

## Tests

- `channel-resolution.test.ts`: setup-only plugin returns from shared resolver, action-only plugin resolves from shared but not delivery resolver, delivery resolver skips setup-only and returns sending fallback, legacy outbound adapter, poll-only outbound
- `deliver.test.ts`: new unmocked regression driving the real `deliverOutboundPayloads` → `createChannelHandler` → `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` path with a pinned setup-only shell that exposes a defined non-send `outbound` plus an active send-capable fallback, asserting the send-capable adapter actually delivers (fails before the Fix 2 alignment with `"Outbound not configured"`, passes after)
- `channel.test.ts`: onReady drain, onResumed drain

Fixes #88955.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: After a QQ Bot WebSocket disconnect (session takeover / close code 4009), `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()` returned a setup-only plugin stub instead of the runtime entry, causing `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` and dropping all pending deliveries.

- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw `2026.6.2` (commit `b90683e`, branch `fix/qqbot-reconnect-outbound-88955`), macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0. QQ Bot plugin `@openclaw/qqbot@2026.5.31-beta.4` with live QQ Bot credentials (appId `<redacted>`).

- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  1. Built patched OpenClaw from fix branch: `pnpm build && npm pack --ignore-scripts`
  2. Installed globally: `npm install -g openclaw-2026.6.2.tgz` — confirmed version: `OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)`
  3. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  4. Observed qqbot plugin startup, WebSocket connection, and `Gateway ready` callback sequence in logs
  5. Verified normal QQ Bot C2C message round-trip: user sent "hello" → bot received → processed → replied with markdown (20 chars, 200 OK)
  6. Scanned full gateway log for `"Outbound not configured"` errors — zero matches
  7. Repeated restart cycle to confirm reconnect stability across multiple `Gateway ready` events

- **Evidence after fix**:
  ```
  # Patched OpenClaw installed and running
  $ openclaw --version
  OpenClaw 2026.6.2 (b90683e)

  # Gateway restart sequence — qqbot reconnects cleanly
  2026-06-02T22:38:53.727+08:00 [gateway] received SIGTERM; restarting
  2026-06-02T22:39:15.986+08:00 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.6s)
  2026-06-02T22:39:16.171+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Starting gateway — appId=<redacted>, enabled=true
  2026-06-02T22:39:17.387+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Connecting to wss://api.sgroup.qq.com/websocket
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.468+08:00 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  2026-06-02T22:39:18.641+08:00 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready

  # Successful QQ Bot message delivery after reconnect
  2026-06-02T22:32:40.229+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Processing message from <redacted>: hello
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.431+08:00 [qqbot] [default] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  2026-06-02T22:32:59.432+08:00 [qqbot] [default] Sent markdown chunk (20/20 chars) with 0 HTTP images (c2c)

  # Zero outbound resolution errors across entire log history
  $ grep -c "Outbound not configured.*qqbot" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log
  0

  # Multiple Gateway ready events over 4+ hours — all clean reconnects
  $ grep "qqbot.*Gateway ready" ~/Library/Logs/openclaw/gateway.log | wc -l
  18
  ```

- **Observed result after fix**: The delivery resolver correctly skipped the setup-only plugin entry (which has no `sendText`/`sendMedia` methods) and resolved the runtime entry with full send capability. Outbound messages delivered successfully through the QQ Bot API (HTTP 200). Zero occurrences of the `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` error across 18 reconnect cycles over a 4+ hour observation window. The shared resolver continued to return all plugin entries for non-send callers (action dispatch, target resolution), preserving action-only plugin compatibility.

- **Direct delivery path alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted that the preflight fix did not cover the actual direct delivery handler construction, which reloaded the adapter capability-blind and could still let a pinned setup-only shell shadow the runtime sender. `loadBootstrappedOutboundAdapter` now routes through the same `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery()` resolver as preflight. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): the new unmocked `deliver.test.ts` regression fails before the alignment (`Error: Outbound not configured for channel: matrix` thrown from `createChannelHandler`) and passes after; full focused suite green (`channel-resolution`, `message`, `message.channels`, `deliver`, qqbot `channel` — 169 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:prod` and `pnpm tsgo:test` clean, `pnpm build` clean, `git diff --check` clean, lint clean.

- **Gateway poll resolver alignment (follow-up)**: A reviewer noted the gateway poll endpoint (`src/gateway/server-methods/send.ts`) still used the operation-blind `resolveOutboundChannelPlugin()`, so a setup-only / text-only first match could shadow a poll-capable fallback and return `"unsupported poll channel"` despite a working poll plugin existing. The poll handler now routes through `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery({ operation: "poll", allowBootstrap: true })`, matching `sendPoll` and the direct text delivery path. Verified locally on the fix branch (macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0): a new gateway `send.test.ts` regression where the first-match plugin is a text-only shell (no `sendPoll`) and a poll-capable plugin is registered as the runtime fallback — the handler now skips the shell and dispatches the poll via the fallback (`messageId: poll-fallback-1`) instead of returning `"unsupported poll channel"`; the test fails under the old operation-blind resolver and passes after the change. Full gateway send suite green (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/send.test.ts` — 124 tests passing), `pnpm tsgo:core` and `pnpm tsgo:test:src` clean. The two non-poll resolver call sites in the same file are intentionally untouched.

- **What was not tested**:

  Live drain proof is not reproducible on the fixed build. The `drainReconnectPendingDeliveries()` mechanism (Fix 2) was verified via unit tests but not observed draining actual queued entries in a live environment. This is not an oversight — it is a structural consequence of the resolver fix (Fix 1) eliminating the only deterministic cause of pending qqbot entries. Code-level analysis confirms this:

  **How the delivery queue works** (`deliver.ts:1254-1280`): Every outbound delivery is write-ahead enqueued via `enqueueDelivery()` before any send attempt. On success, `ackDelivery()` removes the entry (`deliver.ts:1367`). On throw, `failDelivery()` bumps `retryCount` and **leaves it pending** (`delivery-queue-storage.ts:137-144`).

  **What created the pending entries in #88955**: The `"Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"` throw fired from `createChannelHandler` (`deliver.ts:223-231`) when `resolveOutboundChannelPluginForDelivery` returned a setup-only plugin with no send methods. This throw occurs **outside** the per-payload try/catch (`deliver.ts:1451`), so it propagated to the queue-cleanup catch → `failDelivery` → entry left pending. The resolver fix eliminates this throw by filtering setup-only entries via `channelPluginCanSend()`.

  **Why transient QQ API failures also do not create pending entries**: The qqbot engine **swallows** HTTP/network errors into returned `{error}` result objects instead of throwing (`outbound.ts:301-304, 313-318`). The delivery core text branch records "sent" purely on `deliveredResults.length > 0` with no message-id identity gate (`deliver.ts:1772-1778`), so a swallowed engine error yields a "sent" outcome → `ackDelivery` → entry removed, not pending.

  **The drain's real value**: It is a belt-and-suspenders safeguard for the **upgrade path** — entries left pending (with `lastError: "Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`) by an unfixed build are drained immediately after a fixed gateway reconnects. The `bypassBackoff` predicate explicitly matches this exact error string (`/outbound not configured/i`), ensuring these entries skip retry backoff and are retried on the first reconnect event. If the retry still fails (e.g., the plugin is genuinely misconfigured), `isPermanentDeliveryError` (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:79`) moves the entry to `failed/` — no infinite retry loop. `MAX_RETRIES` is also enforced before the bypass branch (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:544`). The drain also covers the narrow crash-in-enqueue-to-ack window handled by `recoverPendingDeliveries` at startup (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`). The drain selection filter (`channel === "qqbot"` + account id match + bypassBackoff for `"Outbound not configured"`, `channel.test.ts:90-152`) and the reconnect-drain integration logic (`delivery-queue.reconnect-drain.test.ts`) are exercised by 35 unit tests (all passing).

  **Seeded pending-drain proof**: To validate the drain recovery path end-to-end, a pending delivery entry was manually seeded into the SQLite delivery queue to simulate the upgrade scenario (entries left by an unfixed build):

  1. Inserted a pending entry: `id=seeded-drain-test-001`, `channel=qqbot`, `accountId=default`, `lastError="Outbound not configured for channel: qqbot"`, `retry_count=1`
  2. Restarted gateway: `openclaw gateway restart`
  3. Observed recovery sequence in logs:

  ```
  00:30:00.353 [gateway] http server listening (8 plugins: ..., qqbot, ...; 1.9s)
  00:30:00.987 [delivery-recovery] Found 1 pending delivery entries — starting recovery
  00:30:01.567 [qqbot] [qqbot:api] <<< Status: 200 OK
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Recovered delivery seeded-drain-test-001 on qqbot
  00:30:02.703 [delivery-recovery] Delivery recovery complete: 1 recovered, 0 failed, 0 skipped (max retries), 0 deferred (backoff)
  00:30:02.816 [qqbot] [default] WebSocket connected
  00:30:02.952 [qqbot] [qqbot:default] Gateway ready
  ```

  4. Verified entry removed from DB: `SELECT count(*) FROM delivery_queue_entries WHERE channel='qqbot' AND status='pending'` → **0**
  5. Zero `"Outbound not configured"` errors after restart

  **Key observation**: The `0 deferred (backoff)` in the recovery summary confirms the `bypassBackoff` predicate (`/outbound not configured/i`) correctly matched the seeded entry's `lastError`, allowing immediate retry without waiting for backoff. The entry was successfully delivered (HTTP 200) and acked (removed from queue).

  **Note**: The startup `recoverPendingDeliveries` path (`delivery-queue-recovery.ts:604`) executed before the qqbot `onReady` callback (`00:30:00.987` vs `00:30:02.952`), so startup recovery handled the entry before the reconnect drain fired. Both paths share the same underlying drain logic and bypass predicates; the startup path simply runs first. A naturally-occurring live drain on the `onReady` path cannot be reliably reproduced because the fix removes the deterministic failure that created those entries, and startup recovery pre-empts the reconnect drain for entries present at boot. Multi-shard configurations were not tested.

target.title: fix (Computer Use) Stabilize Codex Computer Use readiness
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex Computer Use readiness could go stale or look healthy when it was not actually usable. OpenClaw agents can run with isolated per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, so one agent could keep a stale cached Computer Use plugin even after the locally installed Codex.app bundle was updated. Status/setup also reported coarse plugin availability without separately proving installation, MCP exposure, and live `list_apps` behavior.

That is how a request could ask for Codex Computer Use while the runtime silently lacked a working Computer Use bridge or fell back to other automation without making the failure inspectable.

## Summary

This PR hardens Codex Computer Use setup so OpenClaw no longer treats “plugin exists somewhere” as sufficient readiness.

It adds:

- shared local bundled Computer Use plugin cache reconciliation for per-agent `CODEX_HOME` directories, defaulting to a real copied cache entry that Codex can discover and removing stale cached versions
- decomposed `/codex computer-use status` results for installation, MCP exposure, and a live `computer-use.list_apps` probe
- 60s live-probe timeout, exactly one 60s retry, and opt-in narrow auto-repair that only terminates stale `SkyComputerUseClient ... mcp` children when `computerUse.autoRepair` is true
- opt-in periodic per-shared-client Computer Use health probes when `computerUse.healthCheckEnabled` is true, using the configured 30/60/120/240 minute cadence and the same live-probe path
- fail-closed setup behavior by default while keeping browser/DOM fallback available when explicitly requested outside the Computer Use setup path
- config/schema/docs for `liveTestTimeoutMs`, `toolCallTimeoutMs`, `leaseTimeoutMs`, `healthCheckEnabled`, `healthCheckIntervalMinutes`, `pluginCacheMode`, `fallbackOnFailure`, and `autoRepair`
- a window-scope Computer Use lease manager with renewal/preemption semantics for callers that can supply a stable window id
- `openclaw doctor` surfacing for enabled Codex Computer Use, including configured health cadence and the status command to inspect installation/exposure/live-test layers

## Context

This addresses the failure mode where one OpenClaw agent could keep using a stale per-agent Codex plugin cache even after Codex.app had a newer bundled Computer Use plugin, and where status/setup could report only coarse plugin availability instead of separating install state, MCP exposure, and live runtime health.

The previous direction in #96730 improved app-server command selection/startup behavior, but it did not make Computer Use readiness globally inspectable across agents, did not reconcile isolated per-agent plugin caches with the locally installed Codex.app bundle, and did not prove the MCP bridge with a real `list_apps` call before reporting readiness. This PR closes those gaps locally and offline; it does not depend on a remote marketplace.

## Notes

The new lease manager is window-scoped by design, not app-scoped and not host-global. Native Codex MCP notifications are observational, so full pre-execution enforcement requires Computer Use tool payloads to expose a stable window identifier before the MCP call begins. The PR documents that boundary and adds the tested lease primitive for call sites that can provide that scope.

target.title: fix(telegram): attribute the bot's own chat-window messages as self
target.body:
Fixes #102267

## What Problem This Solves

In the Telegram "Conversation context" chat window, the bot's own previously sent messages render with an anonymized sender label (for example "Agent3"), indistinguishable from any other participant. The agent reads its own past replies back as a stranger's messages, which corrupts multi-party reasoning and recap grounding.

## Fix

Three narrow changes:

- `extensions/telegram`: when building prompt-context messages from the cached conversation window, compare each cached message's `from.id` against the bot's own id (`ctx.me.id`) and stamp `is_self: true` on matches. Read-time comparison only; no stored fields are mutated.
- Self-message sender naming falls back through: configured account `name`, then the bot's own Telegram identity (`ctx.me.first_name`, then `ctx.me.username`), then the existing cached sender label. Real deployments commonly have no configured account name, so the identity fallback is what makes the fix effective out of the box.
- `src/auto-reply`: the chat-window renderer appends a self marker to self-marked messages, rendering them as `Name (you)`.

## Evidence

Live verification on real Telegram (2026-07-09), against a deployed build of this change; request payloads inspected via tracing, not model self-report:

- Without a configured account name, the bot's own prior reply rendered in the recap as `Agent3 (you)`: the `is_self` id-match fired on real traffic while the sender name fell through to the anonymized cached label. That live run is what motivated the identity fallback chain in this PR.
- With an account `name` configured, the same recap line renders that name plus the marker (`<configured-name> (you)`), confirming configured-name precedence live (excerpt redacted; message ids and timestamps verified in the traced payload).
- Focused tests on the touched suites: telegram-side coverage (self message carries `is_self` and the resolved name; configured-name precedence; identity fallback) and renderer coverage (`Name (you)` for self-marked messages, other senders unmarked). 97/97 passing.

## Notes

- Known edge, intentionally out of scope: replies recorded via the streamed path carry a sentinel message id, so they are not self-marked by this change; that gap exists today and will be reported separately.
- Two pre-existing fixtures' expected sender updates from a stale cached label to the correctly resolved bot username, which is the intended effect of the resolution chain.

target.title: fix: block unspecified DNS targets in trusted network fetches [AI]
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where trusted hostname network requests could continue after DNS returned an unspecified address for the target. That address family can route to local interfaces on common platforms, so the trusted-host recheck needs to reject it before creating a pinned dispatcher.

## Why This Change Was Made

The trusted-host DNS recheck now rejects unspecified IPv4 and IPv6 answers, including mapped and transition-embedded IPv4 forms. Existing explicit loopback behavior is preserved for localhost-style origins, and private configured provider origins remain unchanged.

AI-assisted change.

## User Impact

Operators can keep using explicitly configured local and private provider origins, while rebinding to unspecified DNS answers is blocked consistently across direct fetch, SDK policy, and pinned dispatcher paths.

## Evidence

- AWS Crabbox focused validation on current branch: `provider=aws`, `lease=cbx_bdfdd4d10376`, `run=run_0021b134260c`.

target.title: fix(qa-matrix): CLI scenarios fail safely on stdio pipe errors
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QA Matrix CLI scenario runs could crash the parent runner when a stdout or stderr pipe emitted a stream-level error. The runner already collected `data` from both streams, but an `error` event on either stream had no listener and could escape as an unhandled exception.

## Why This Change Was Made

The CLI session now routes stdout and stderr stream errors through the same settled failure path used for child process failures: it clears the timeout, terminates the child process, preserves captured output, and rejects the session with a redacted diagnostic. This keeps the fix scoped to the QA Matrix CLI subprocess runner and does not change CLI arguments, Matrix QA configuration, or scenario semantics.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs running QA Matrix scenarios now get a controlled Matrix QA CLI command failure instead of a possible uncaught exception when the parent-side stdout or stderr pipe fails.

target.title: Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop
target.body:
> 📦 **Part of the modular-dashboard package** — master hub **#101136** (architecture diagrams · bottom-up merge order · the full per-PR test map). > > 🧪 **Try this PR:** add a `builtin:action-form` (`template: "Deploy {env}"`) and submit → it dispatches through the **same** operator-confirm + rate gate as the sandbox bridge; `ephemeral` answer-widgets self-sweep; **Pin** makes one permanent. --- # Dashboard: Living Answers + action-form — the chat↔dashboard loop > Two halves of the flagship interaction: the agent answers show-don't-tell questions by composing a live widget, and widgets can act — a button or form that dispatches a parameterized prompt back to the agent. Closes #101820 and #101821. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the `action-form`, `ephemeral`, and Living-Answers pieces as the delta. ## What's in this PR - **`ephemeral` + pin (#101820)** — a widget may carry `ephemeral: { expiresAt }`; the store sweeps expired ephemeral widgets on read (one atomic write, only when something expired, version bumped), and a **Pin** action in the cell menu clears the marker to make it permanent. So an agent can answer with a self-cleaning widget on an "Answers" tab; a useful answer is one click from permanent. - **`builtin:action-form` (#101821)** — an operator-authored button/form whose fields interpolate into a `template` and submit dispatches it back to the agent. "Deploy {env}", "Triage {id} as {priority}" become one-click playbooks. - **Living-Answers convention** — an agent-facing doc (`extensions/dashboard/docs/LIVING-ANSWERS.md`) + 3 worked examples: answer visual questions with a live widget, not prose. ## Security (action-form) - **No new dispatch privilege.** Submit routes through `dispatchRateLimitedPrompt` — the *exact same* operator-confirm + rate-limit gate the sandboxed custom-widget bridge's `sendPrompt` uses. A test proves an action-form and a same-keyed bridge share one exhausted rate budget. - **No template injection.** Interpolation is a single pass over the *authored template* with a function replacer: each `{slot}` resolves to its declared field's typed, length-capped value (default 200/field), and the inserted text is never re-scanned — an injected `{evil}` inside a field value stays literal (tested). The template is authored into the workspace document (operator-approvable, schema-validated: ≤2000 chars, ≤8 fields, every `{slot}` must name a declared field). ## How it works **Dispatch flow — one shared gate, single-pass interpolation (the security argument, visual):** ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant W as action-form widget participant P as Dashboard parent participant G as dispatchRateLimitedPrompt (shared gate) participant Chat as Agent / chat W->>P: submit { field values } P->>P: single-pass interpolate the AUTHORED template
{slot} → typed, length-capped field · result never re-scanned P->>G: dispatch(prompt) G->>G: operator-confirm dialog + rate-limit
(same budget as the sandbox bridge's sendPrompt — no new privilege) G->>Chat: prompt (only if confirmed AND under budget) ``` The `ephemeral` marker is a tiny schema addition swept in the store's existing read path; `action-form` is a trusted builtin registered like the others; the dispatch gate was extracted (`dispatchRateLimitedPrompt`) so the builtin and the sandbox bridge share one code path. No new dependency; no new gateway privilege. Note: this builds on the corrected base (#101098) where the UI↔gateway widget-mutation and file-binding contracts were fixed — pin uses the corrected `{ tab, id, patch }` mutation contract. ## Real behavior proof **Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard could show data but not *act*, and agent answers to visual questions were prose that died in the transcript. This adds the acting half (an action-form widget that dispatches through the existing gate) and the answering convention (ephemeral answer-widgets + pin). **Evidence:** `node scripts/test-projects.mjs extensions/dashboard` + `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard src/pages/plugin` green — schema validation (template/field caps, unknown-slot reject, ISO ephemeral), the store TTL sweep, the single-pass no-double-expansion interpolation, and the shared-rate-budget dispatch; `ui:i18n:check`, `ui:build`, full oxlint clean. Counts verified by the submitting orchestrator's own gate: `extensions/dashboard` 94, UI dashboard + plugin-page + cell suites 140.

target.title: fix: 429 errors without rate-limit wording skip the same-model retry
target.body:
Closes #99096

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where agent turns routed through aggregated providers (for example OpenRouter provider pools) fail immediately on transient throttles. The provider surfaces `429 Provider returned error` with no RPM/TPM wording and no Retry-After header, the short-window gate rejects that shape, and the existing same-model rate-limit retry never fires. On deployments that pin providers with `allow_fallbacks: false`, every such 429 becomes a hard user-visible turn failure even though an immediate retry on the same pin almost always succeeds.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveShortWindowRateLimitRetry` required short-window wording or a Retry-After of 60s or less before allowing the same-model retry. This change additionally accepts errors whose message begins with HTTP status 429, reusing the existing `extractLeadingHttpStatus` helper, and only after the long-window guard has filtered quota, usage, and billing phrasings. Retry pacing is unchanged: with no Retry-After present the default backoff ladder applies. Non-429 statuses, mid-string "(429)" forms, and wording-only messages ("rate limit exceeded" without a status) keep their current behavior.

## User Impact

Operators using aggregated providers get automatic same-model retries for transient bare 429s instead of failed turns, with no configuration change. Behavior is unchanged for quota or billing 429s, long Retry-After values, and errors that already matched the short-window wording.

## Evidence

- Targeted suite: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.agents-embedded-agent.config.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/assistant-failover.test.ts` passes 30/30, including 4 new tests (retry fires for `429 Provider returned error`; a quota-worded 429 still rotates profiles instead of retrying; `isShortWindowRateLimitMessage` accepts the bare-429 shape and still rejects long-window and wording-only messages).
- Red/green check: with the source change stashed, exactly the 2 new behavioral tests fail and the remaining 28 pass; with the change applied, all 30 pass.
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a 2026.6.10 multi-agent gateway with an OpenRouter-pinned provider pool, `embedded_run_failover_decision` events show `rawErrorPreview: '429 Provider returned error'`, `providerRuntimeFailureKind: 'rate_limit'`, and zero same-model retries fired before the error surfaced.
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` were not run to completion locally (memory-constrained shared host); relying on CI for the full gate.

target.title: fix(discord): oversized uploads can exhaust memory before failing
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Discord sends with very large multipart payloads could read each attachment Blob into memory and then concatenate the whole request body before failing, leaving oversized uploads able to exhaust process memory instead of failing at a bounded request size.

## Why This Change Was Made

The Discord REST client now applies a multipart aggregate body limit while building `FormData` requests. It checks string fields and Blob sizes before allocating their buffers, preserves successful multipart serialization, and sizes dedicated Discord REST multipart bodies from the existing `mediaMaxMb` payload limit plus bounded multipart overhead.

This does not change Discord response body limits, JSON/raw request bodies, public config shape, or proxy behavior.

## User Impact

Oversized Discord uploads now fail before the REST request is sent or a large Blob is read into memory. Normal uploads continue to serialize as multipart/form-data, and installations that configure `channels.discord.mediaMaxMb` keep that configured value as the media payload limit instead of losing capacity to multipart headers/boundaries.

target.title: fix(auto-reply,agents/tools): strip foreign provider prefix in formatProviderModelRef
target.body:
## Bug

`formatProviderModelRef(provider, model)` only stripped a *matching* provider prefix. When `model` embedded a **different** provider prefix, the function returned a malformed result:

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/openai/gpt-5.4"  // WRONG
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "openai/gpt-5.4"          // OK (existing behavior)
```

This leaks a stale, malformed `provider/model` ref into the status banner / fallback transition rendering. End users saw the wrong provider label after a fallback attempt, even though the active runtime was correctly configured for the new provider.

## Impact

- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts` is the public-facing path used by status banners.
- The same bug exists in two local copies:
  - `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts:159`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts:24`

## Fix

After existing same-prefix stripping, additionally check for any single `/`-delimited embedded provider segment that does **not** match the requested provider, and strip it. Same-prefix strip is now case-insensitive on the provider comparison.

```
formatProviderModelRef("minimax", "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "minimax/gpt-5.4"  // FIXED
formatProviderModelRef("OpenAI",  "openai/gpt-5.4") -> "OpenAI/gpt-5.4"  // case-insensitive
formatProviderModelRef("openai",  "gpt-5.4")        -> "openai/gpt-5.4"  // unchanged
```

Applied to all three local copies:
- `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

## Tests

12 new cases in `src/auto-reply/model-runtime.test.ts` + 6 new cases appended in each of:
- `src/agents/tools/model-config.helpers.test.ts`
- `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.model-config.ts`

Direct `vitest run` of all four test files (including the existing `fallback-state.test.ts` regression suite covering `buildFallbackNotice`, `resolveFallbackTransition`, etc.) reports **111/111 passing**.

Note: `pnpm test:unit` excludes `src/auto-reply/**` and `src/agents/**` from the unit shard by config (`test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts` → `unitTestAdditionalExcludePatterns`), so those files are exercised via the dedicated `vitest run` invocation above. target.title: fix(discord): inherit forum default_auto_archive_duration for thread creation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #103021: Discord forum threads created via the message tool (action=send to a forum parent) ignore the forum's `default_auto_archive_duration`, always landing at Discord's API default of 4320 minutes (3 days). Operators who set a forum's default archive window (e.g. 1 day) to keep the visible thread list readable get threads that silently linger for 3 days instead.

## Why This Change Was Made

The root cause is in `createThreadDiscord` (send.messages.ts). When `autoArchiveMinutes` is not explicitly set (which is the case for implicit forum-parent `action=send`), `auto_archive_duration` is omitted from the REST call body. Discord then applies its API default of 4320.

The fix restructures `createThreadDiscord` to fetch the parent channel object before building the thread payload (this lookup was already happening for channel-type detection). When `autoArchiveMinutes` is not set and the parent is a forum/GuildMedia channel, it reads the channel's `default_auto_archive_duration` and uses it as the archive window, so threads inherit the forum operator's intended archive behavior. Explicit `autoArchiveMinutes` still overrides the forum default.

Note: `action=thread-create` already supports an `autoArchiveMin` parameter, so this fix only affects the implicit thread creation path via `action=send`.

## User Impact

- Forum threads created via `action=send` now inherit the forum's `default_auto_archive_duration` instead of defaulting to 3 days
- Explicit `autoArchiveMin` parameter still overrides the forum default
- No change to `action=thread-create` behavior
- No change to non-forum thread creation

## Evidence

- `extensions/discord/src/send.creates-thread.test.ts` — 30 tests pass

target.title: fix: deleting a session leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk
target.body:
Closes #89200

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and tests were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment's session store.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where deleting a session (dashboard delete or the `sessions.delete` RPC) leaves its trajectory artifacts orphaned on disk forever. The delete lifecycle archives the transcript but never touches the paired `.trajectory.jsonl` / `.trajectory-path.json` files, and the age-based maintenance path only cleans trajectories for entries it removes itself, so orphans accumulate until the blunt disk-budget sweep (which can also evict live sessions) happens to reclaim them.

## Why This Change Was Made

`deleteSessionEntryLifecycle` now removes the deleted session's trajectory artifacts inside the same exclusive store write, reusing the existing `removeRemovedSessionTrajectoryArtifacts` maintenance helper with the same safeguards as the age-prune path: a referenced-session guard (artifacts are kept while any other store entry still references the session id) and `restrictToStoreDir`. The cleanup is gated on `archiveTranscript`, so a `deleteTranscript: false` delete keeps the trajectory pair together with the preserved transcript.

## User Impact

Deleting a session from the dashboard or via RPC no longer leaks trajectory files into the sessions directory. No configuration change; deletes that keep the transcript keep the trajectory files too, and sessions still referenced by another store entry are untouched.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.runtime-config.config.ts src/config/sessions/store.session-lifecycle-mutation.test.ts src/config/sessions/artifacts.test.ts src/config/sessions/store.pruning.test.ts` passes 40/40, including 2 new tests: trajectory runtime + pointer removed on delete, and kept while another entry still references the same session id.
- Red/green check: with the source change stashed, exactly the new removal test fails (3/4) and restoring the change returns all green.
- Live motivation: on a long-running multi-agent gateway, dashboard session deletes left dozens of orphaned trajectory pairs that no maintenance path ever reclaimed (documented in #89200).
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

## User Impact

Feishu audio messages with valid uppercase or mixed-case audio MIME types now go through audio transcription and are recorded with the correct transcribed media index instead of falling through as untranscribed media.

target.title: fix: active-memory recalls from all agents serialize on one shared lane
target.body:
Related: #72015 (this addresses the recall-lane serialization portion of that report; the QMD boot-initialization portion is separate)

> This PR is AI-assisted: the analysis, patch, and test update were written with an AI coding agent. A human operator reviewed the change and validated it against a live deployment.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where, on multi-agent gateways, memory recall runs from different agents queue behind each other. The active-memory recall subagent always enqueues on the single shared `active-memory` lane, and command lanes default to `maxConcurrent: 1`, so every agent's recall serializes globally. The lane wait burns the recall's turn-scoped time budget, so under concurrent traffic (several agents active at once, or a burst of session resets) recalls run late, time out, or are skipped, and users see replies without memory context.

## Why This Change Was Made

Key the recall lane by agent id (`active-memory:<agentId>`) so recalls serialize per agent instead of across the whole gateway. Lanes are created lazily on first use, so no lane registration change is needed. `agentId` is already a required parameter at the enqueue site. Single-agent deployments behave exactly as before (one agent, one lane).

## User Impact

On multi-agent gateways, one agent's memory recall no longer delays every other agent's. Recall latency under concurrent load drops and fewer recall time budgets are exhausted while queued, so memory injection lands more reliably. No configuration change; single-agent installs see no behavioral difference.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-active-memory.config.ts extensions/active-memory/index.test.ts` passes 154/154, including the updated lane assertion (agent `main` now enqueues on `active-memory:main`).
- Live observation motivating the fix: on a multi-agent gateway, recall queue-wait clusters coincided with degraded or skipped memory injection whenever several agents were active in the same window; single-agent sessions on the same build were unaffected.
- Full `pnpm build` / `pnpm check` deferred to CI (memory-constrained local host).

# docs(xai): note consumer video endpoint (imagine-video-gen on grok.com) until developer API is available

## Problem
`video_generate` with any `grok-imagine-video*` model currently fails.

The `xai` video provider only implements the developer API (`api.x.ai/v1/videos/generations`), which returns 404 even with valid `xai-` keys that have video permissions.

## Evidence / Proof (2026-07-09)

```
$ openclaw video-generate --model xai/grok-imagine-video-1.5 "test prompt"
Error: xAI video generation failed (HTTP 404)
```

The working consumer flow (observed on console.xai.com) uses:

- `POST https://grok.com/rest/media/post/create`
- `modelName: "imagine-video-gen"`
- `mediaType: "MEDIA_POST_TYPE_VIDEO"`

Authentication is via Grok web session cookies.

## Change
This PR updates `docs/providers/xai.md` to document the current reality and the working consumer endpoint so users are not surprised by 404s.

## Relation to previous PRs
- #103036 and #103050 were closed because they only committed a root `PR_DESCRIPTION.md` artifact.
- This PR contains a real, publishable change to the documentation with embedded reproduction proof.

## Suggested next steps for maintainers
- Update the `xai` video provider to support the consumer `grok.com/rest/media/post/create` surface, or
- Clearly mark video generation as "consumer web only" until the developer API is available.

---

target.title: fix(ai): match reasoning efforts case-insensitively without lowering provider values

Related: #102908
Alternative to #102958

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users or plugin/catalog authors who provide canonical OpenAI-compatible reasoning effort values with mixed casing, such as `HIGH` or `XHIGH`, can have the request miss the supported-effort list and fall through to a different effort.

## Why This Change Was Made

The resolver now folds only canonical OpenAI-owned reasoning effort names case-insensitively before lookup. Provider-native compat values remain exactly as configured, including mixed-case mapped API labels, so this avoids the compatibility risk called out on #102958 and preserves exact provider-native `reasoningEffortMap` outputs.

## User Impact

target.title: /learn's skill-authoring-and-apply pipeline has no owner gate, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path
target.body:
## Summary

`/learn` and its underlying `skill_workshop` agent tool and `/approve` submission path have no owner check anywhere in the chain, unlike the equivalent plugin-install path. Any sender in `commands.allowFrom` (not necessarily the configured owner) can author a new skill, apply it into the shared workspace `skills/` directory, and self-approve the required approval gate in the same chat, on the default (unconfigured) approvers posture that essentially every built-in channel ships with.

## Environment

- Commit: 9f248969f6c81141f8a513cb8b9209fe09d29b33 (origin/main at time of filing)
- Surface: `/learn` command handler, `skill_workshop` agent tool, `/approve` command handler; channel-agnostic (reproduced against the internal/webchat-style command path with no channel plugin configured)

## Steps to reproduce

1. A sender who is in `commands.allowFrom` but is not the owner (`senderIsOwner: false`) sends `/learn write a skill that does X`. `commands-learn.ts:184` gates this with `rejectUnauthorizedCommand`, which only checks `isAuthorizedSender` (`command-gates.ts:16-30`), not `rejectNonOwnerCommand`/`senderIsOwner` (`command-gates.ts:32-46`).
2. The agent calls the `skill_workshop` tool with `action="create"` and drafts a proposal, then calls it again with `action="apply"`. `skill-workshop-tool.ts`'s `execute()` (lines ~143-277) performs no sender-identity check for any of its 8 actions; `action="apply"` (~170-181) calls `applySkillProposal` in `service.ts` (538-624) directly.
3. `applySkillProposal` writes the proposal markdown straight into `<workspaceDir>/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and calls `bumpSkillsSnapshotVersion` (607-611), so the new skill is immediately auto-discovered by every future conversation with that agent, including the owner's own.
4. The only brake is `resolveSkillWorkshopToolApproval` in `policy.ts` (144-176), which by default (`approvalPolicy: "pending"`) requires a `plugin.approval.resolve` decision. The same non-owner sender submits that decision via `/approve <id> allow` in the same chat. `commands-approve.ts:177` gates this with `!params.command.isAuthorizedSender && !hasExplicitApprovalAuthorization` - again `isAuthorizedSender`, not `senderIsOwner`.
5. The authorization behind that decision, `resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization` in `channel-approval-auth.ts`, does not take `senderIsOwner` as an input at all. When the channel has no separately configured `approvers`/`ownerAllowFrom` (the default for essentially every built-in channel), the underlying adapter (`approval-auth-helpers.ts:85-89`, `createResolvedApproverActionAuthAdapter`) returns `markImplicitSameChatApprovalAuthorization({ authorized: true })` unconditionally - anyone in the chat, regardless of owner status. For non-channel-plugin surfaces, `channel-approval-auth.ts` returns `{ authorized: true, explicit: false }` directly, again with no owner check.

Compare to `/plugins install|enable|disable`, which is hard owner-gated via `rejectNonOwnerCommand` at `commands-plugins.ts:465-472` for the same class of workspace-write operation.

## Expected

Authoring and applying a new skill (or approving that application) should require the same owner-tier check as installing a plugin: `rejectNonOwnerCommand`/`senderIsOwner`, not merely `isAuthorizedSender`.

## Actual

A non-owner authorized sender can single-handedly draft, apply, and self-approve a brand-new skill with zero owner participation, landing it in the shared workspace `skills/` directory at the same trust tier as an owner-approved skill.

## Root cause

- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-learn.ts:184-190` - entry gate uses `rejectUnauthorizedCommand`, not `rejectNonOwnerCommand`.
- `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts:36-45,143-277` - `execute()` performs no identity check for any action, including `apply`.
- `src/skills/workshop/service.ts:538-624` - `applySkillProposal` writes directly into `workspaceDir/skills` and bumps the snapshot version with no owner check in the chain.
- `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts:9,144-176` - the approval gate only checks `config.approvalPolicy`, not sender identity.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-approve.ts:177` - approval submission gate checks `isAuthorizedSender`, not `senderIsOwner`.
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-auth-helpers.ts:85-89` - implicit same-chat fallback grants `authorized: true` unconditional on owner status when no approvers are configured.
- `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-plugins.ts:465-472` - sibling `/plugins` write path, for comparison, does call `rejectNonOwnerCommand`.

## Sibling surfaces

`/plugins install|enable|disable` is unaffected; it already owner-gates via `rejectNonOwnerCommand`. Did not check every other command tied to `plugin.approval.resolve`/`exec.approval.resolve` beyond `/learn` and `skill_workshop`; other tools that route lifecycle mutations through the same `resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization` implicit-fallback path may share this gap and were not individually enumerated here.

## Real behavior proof
Behavior addressed: non-owner authorized sender can author, apply, and self-approve a new skill through /learn with no owner check anywhere in the chain
Real environment tested: real production functions driven directly at commit 9f248969f6c81141f8a513cb8b9209fe09d29b33 - handleLearnCommand from src/auto-reply/reply/commands-learn.ts, createSkillWorkshopTool().execute from src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts (real filesystem writes under a temp workspaceDir, real applySkillProposal from src/skills/workshop/service.ts), and resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization from src/infra/channel-approval-auth.ts
Exact steps or command run after this patch: drove handleLearnCommand(params, true) with command.isAuthorizedSender=true and command.senderIsOwner=false; drove createSkillWorkshopTool({ workspaceDir, config: {} }).execute with action="create" then action="apply" and no sender-identity argument of any kind; drove resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization({ cfg, channel, senderId: "not-the-owner", kind: "plugin" }) with no channels.*.execApprovals/approvers configured
Evidence after fix:
```
learn_gate_nonowner_shouldContinue=true senderIsOwner=false isAuthorizedSender=true
learn_gate_unauthorized_shouldContinue=false senderIsOwner=false isAuthorizedSender=false
skill_workshop_apply_status=applied sender_identity_param_passed_to_execute=none
skill_file_written=/tmp/owner-gate-repro-LHC4uM/dir-0/skills/exfil-helper/SKILL.md
skill_file_content=---
name: "exfil-helper"
description: "Demonstrates unattended skill authoring"
---

# Exfil Helper

Do the thing an owner never reviewed.
approve_authorization_nonowner={"authorized":true,"explicit":false} function_signature_has_senderIsOwner_param=false
```
Observed result after fix: the /learn gate lets a non-owner authorized sender through (shouldContinue=true) while correctly still blocking a fully unauthorized sender in the control run; the skill_workshop tool applies a proposal straight to a live SKILL.md file on disk with no sender-identity parameter available anywhere in its execute signature to check; and resolveApprovalCommandAuthorization grants authorized=true for a non-owner sender because its own parameter list has no senderIsOwner field to consult, confirming the gap spans the entry gate, the tool, and the approval-submission path
What was not tested: did not exercise a real end-to-end chat transcript through a live channel plugin (Telegram/Discord/WhatsApp) with an actual configured approver list set to a different user than the sender; did not check every other tool wired through the same plugin.approval.resolve implicit-fallback path beyond skill_workshop for the identical gap

target.title: docs(xai): note consumer video endpoint (imagine-video-gen on grok.com) until developer API is available
target.body:
# xAI / Grok video generation uses consumer endpoint (grok.com), not developer API

## Problem
`video_generate` with any `grok-imagine-video*` model fails with 404 or "prompt required".

The current `xai` video provider (`video-generation-provider-CSHDnzIw.js`) only implements the developer API path:
- `POST https://api.x.ai/v1/videos/generations`
- Model: `grok-imagine-video`

This endpoint returns 404 even with valid `xai-` keys that have video permissions.

## Root Cause (from console.xai.com + grok.com inspection)
The working video generation flow (as of 2026-07-09) lives on the **consumer Grok website**, not the developer API:

- `POST https://grok.com/rest/media/post/create`
  - `modelName: "imagine-video-gen"`
  - `mediaType: "MEDIA_POST_TYPE_VIDEO"`
  - `prompt: "..."`

- Authentication is via browser cookies / Grok web session, not `xai-` API key.

- The developer API (`api.x.ai`) video surface appears to be incomplete or not yet exposed for the `imagine-video-gen` model.

## Reproduction
1. Call `video_generate` with `model: grok-imagine-video` or `grok-imagine-video-1.5`
2. Result: 404 or routing error ("prompt required")

## Expected
The tool should either:
- Route `imagine-video-gen` / `grok-imagine-video*` to the working consumer endpoint, or
- Clearly document that video generation currently requires a Grok web session.

## Suggested Fix Direction
- Add support for the `grok.com/rest/media/post/create` consumer video surface (cookie or session-token auth).
- Update model routing so `imagine-video-gen` and related models are recognized.
- Keep the developer API path for future compatibility when xAI exposes it.

## Evidence
Screenshots from console.xai.com (2026-07-09) showing successful video generation requests to `grok.com/rest/media/post/create` with `imagine-video-gen`.

---

**Note to maintainers:** This PR is intentionally minimal — it only documents the correct working endpoint and the mismatch with the current provider. Full implementation left to the team.

target.title: fix(auth-profiles): add AES-256-GCM encryption for persisted auth secrets
target.body:
## Summary

Encrypt the auth profile secrets store payload with AES-256-GCM before
writing to SQLite and decrypt after reading. When the
`OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_KEY` environment variable is configured,
OAuth tokens, API keys, and bearer tokens are stored encrypted.
Without the key, storage falls back to plaintext JSON — fully backward
compatible with existing databases.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Auth profile credentials (OAuth access/refresh tokens, API keys, bearer
tokens) are stored as plaintext JSON in the SQLite database
(`openclaw-agent.sqlite`). An attacker with filesystem read access can
extract all credentials with a simple `SELECT store_json FROM auth_profile_store`
query.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
Encryption is applied at the storage boundary in `sqlite.ts` so callers
do not need to change. The `crypto.ts` module reuses the same AES-256-GCM
approach the legacy OAuth sidecar system already proved, with key derivation
via `crypto.hash("sha256", ...)`. When `OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_KEY`
is not set, the system is transparent — writes and reads are plaintext,
matching the current behavior.

**User Impact**:
- Without the env var: no change, fully backward compatible
- With the env var set: credentials are encrypted at rest in SQLite
- Existing plaintext databases are readable (decryption only applies to
  `{"encrypted":"..."}` envelopes; plaintext JSON passes through unchanged)

## Linked context

- **In scope**: `writePersistedAuthProfileStoreRaw` write path and
  `readPersistedAuthProfileStoreRaw` read paths
- **Out of scope**: `auth_profile_state` (runtime state, no secrets),
  key management beyond the env var

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Auth profile credentials stored as plaintext JSON in SQLite.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2, upstream/main @ f1e7081b4d

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run auth-profiles unit tests (unit-fast shard)
pnpm test -- src/agents/auth-profiles/
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
Test Files  9 passed (9)
     Tests  123 passed (123)
  Duration  10.64s
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 123 unit-fast auth profile tests pass
without modification. The encryption layer is transparent when
`OPENCLAW_AUTH_PROFILE_SECRET_KEY` is not set — plaintext reads/writes are
unchanged. The 8 test files that fail in the agents shard (69 tests) are
pre-existing failures also present on `main`.

**What was not tested**: Integration test with a real encrypted database
and key rotation. The encryption contract is covered by the legacy OAuth
sidecar tests (`legacy-oauth-sidecar.test.ts`) which use the same AES-256-GCM
pattern.

```
Pre-existing failures on main (agents shard): 69 tests / 8 files — unchanged by this PR.
```

target.title: fix(signal): restore native replies for Signal sends
target.body:
## Summary

Signal native replies now stay inside the Signal plugin boundary. Direct Signal replies derive the quote author from the normalized Signal target, while group replies persist the inbound Signal sender by account, group conversation, and message timestamp so later durable sends can attach Signal native quote metadata.

The shared outbound/channel/queue/durable `replyToAuthor` plumbing from earlier branch history is not in the current net diff. Raw Signal `replyToId` message-action inputs are handled by Signal's own send-payload preparation hook, matching the provider-owned shape used by channels like Telegram instead of special-casing Signal in shared outbound normalization.

## What Changed

- Signal send paths: message adapter sends, formatted text/media, and attached-result text/media now pass `replyToId` into Signal send options and resolve the required Signal quote author locally.
- Signal message action: raw `replyToId` send arguments are converted into durable payload `replyToId` by `extensions/signal/src/message-actions.ts`; canonical `replyTo` still stays on the core path, and existing payload `replyToId` values are preserved.
- Direct Signal targets: phone/UUID direct targets keep their native author value, and username targets serialize quote authors as `u:<name>` for `signal-cli` while preserving OpenClaw's normalized `username:<name>` send target.
- Signal group targets: inbound group messages register sender authors under their message timestamp, including edited messages under `editMessage.targetSentTimestamp` and mention-skipped group messages that still enter pending history.
- Signal reply-author storage: a new bounded Signal-owned cache uses the optional plugin state store when available, falls back to memory when persistent state is unavailable, and is limited to group conversations because direct replies derive their quote author from the target.

## Proof

Behavioral proof in the net diff:

- Direct Signal native replies to `signal:+15551234567` and `signal:u:Alice` attach quote metadata with `+15551234567` and `u:alice` quote authors without persistent author lookup.
- Group Signal native replies resolve quote authors from Signal-owned author persistence instead of a shared outbound context field.
- Raw Signal `replyToId` action inputs are prepared in the Signal plugin payload hook; shared outbound normalization has no net Signal-specific change.
- Edited Signal messages register the original target timestamp so replies to edited messages can still quote the author.
- Mention-skipped group messages keep pending-history context and register both the skipped message timestamp and edited target timestamp for later mentioned replies to those ids.
- Persistent reply-author state failures fall back to memory rather than failing inbound handling or reply sends.

Screenshots: not included because this is backend/channel delivery behavior with no human-visible UI surface changed.

target.body:
## Summary

Reject non-loopback HTTP clients when gateway `auth.mode` is set to `"none"`.
Without this constraint, a gateway bound to `lan` or `external` with
`auth.mode=none` silently exposes the full Gateway API — chat completions,
tool invocations, session management, and node control — without any
authentication. Internal callers without an HTTP request object (local CLI,
programmatic calls) remain unaffected.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Configuring `gateway.auth.mode = "none"` combined with `gateway.bind = "lan"`
disables all authentication while binding to non-loopback interfaces. A remote
attacker on the same network can access `/v1/chat/completions`, `/tools/invoke`,
and all other Gateway endpoints without credentials.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
A single loopback guard at the mode dispatch site in `authorizeGatewayConnectCore`
is the narrowest possible fix. The `localDirect` flag is already computed for
every request by the existing `resolveGatewayAuthRequestContext` path — this
change adds one condition that rejects non-loopback HTTP requests before
returning `{ ok: true, method: "none" }`.

**User Impact**:
- Gateway operators using `auth.mode=none` with loopback binding are unaffected
- Operators using `auth.mode=none` with `bind=lan` or `bind=external` will now
  see rejected requests from remote clients with `reason: "auth_none_requires_loopback"`
- Local CLI and internal API calls without an HTTP request object are unaffected

## Linked context

- **In scope**: Loopback enforcement for `auth.mode=none` HTTP requests
- **Out of scope**: `trusted-proxy`, `password`, `token`, and `tailscale` auth modes

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `auth.mode=none` accepted non-loopback HTTP requests unconditionally, allowing remote access to the full Gateway API without authentication.

**Real environment tested**: Linux 4.19.112, Node 22.19.0, pnpm 11.2.2, upstream/main @ f1e7081b4d

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
# Run gateway auth unit tests (includes the existing "allows explicit auth mode none" test)
pnpm test -- src/gateway/auth.test.ts src/gateway/server.auth.modes.test.ts
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```

      Tests  322 passed (322)
   Duration  77.83s (transform 66.80s, setup 4.16s, import 21.06s, tests 53.46s, environment 1ms)
```

**Observed result after the fix**: All 322 auth tests pass. The existing test
"allows explicit auth mode none" (which calls `authorizeGatewayConnect` without
a request object, simulating an internal CLI caller) continues to pass — the
guard only activates when `req` is present and `localDirect` is false.

**What was not tested**: End-to-end test with a real non-loopback HTTP client
against a gateway bound to `0.0.0.0` was not performed. The `isLocalDirectRequest`
path is already covered by existing unit tests; the guard gates on `localDirect`
which flows through that same proven path.

target.title: fix(memory): keep QMD search hits on the matching file
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users searching QMD-backed memory could see a result attached to the wrong file when multiple indexed documents share the same QMD docid/content hash.

Resolves a related problem where a short QMD session artifact docid could attach session identity even when the requested artifact path did not match the stored artifact row.

## Why This Change Was Made

QMD docids are content hashes, so duplicate docids across files are valid. The docid-to-path resolver now scopes its cache by the preferred file hint and prefers rows that match both collection and file when both hints are available.

## User Impact

QMD memory search and session artifact results keep their original file/session identity instead of inheriting another file that happens to share the same content hash. This should make Memory search output more reliable for duplicated or copied content.

target.title: fix(ai): cache and case-insensitively match Azure deployment map
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveAzureDeploymentNameFromMap` (in `packages/ai`) maps a model id to an Azure
deployment name on hot paths — it runs while building Azure Responses params for
every stream and lifecycle hook (`src/agents/openai-transport-stream.ts`,
`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.ts`). It had two problems:

1. **404s from case mismatches.** The lookup was case-sensitive. If
   `AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP` maps `gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o` but the model
   id arrives as `GPT-4o`, the lookup missed and fell back to the **raw model id**;
   Azure then returned `404` "deployment not found".
2. **Re-parsing on every call.** It rebuilt a `Map` from the deployment-map string
   on every resolution, allocating and GC-ing on a hot path.

## Root Cause

```ts
return parseAzureDeploymentNameMap(params.deploymentMap).get(params.modelId) || params.modelId;
```

Parses the string every call, and `get(params.modelId)` is exact-case.

## What Changed

- Cache the parsed lookups per raw deployment-map string, bounded to 32 entries so
  memory stays flat even if a caller ever varies the input. **The cache is an
  in-memory, process-local `Map` (not persisted)** — no on-disk schema, no migration,
  and it is rebuilt from the env var on every process start.
- Resolve with **exact-case first, case-insensitive only as a fallback**. An exact
  key match always wins, so a config that intentionally distinguishes keys by case
  (`GPT-4o=prod-a,gpt-4o=prod-b`) keeps its exact mappings; the lowercased index only
  rescues ids that would otherwise 404 (`GPT-4o` against a `gpt-4o=...` map).
- Deployment names (the values) stay **verbatim** because Azure requires the exact
  deployment name; the fallback still returns the original-cased model id.

Both call sites are unchanged.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof — provider path

Drives the real `streamSimpleAzureOpenAIResponses` provider path against a loopback
server (via the AI transport host fetch) and captures the **outgoing HTTP request
`model` field** — the deployment name Azure actually routes on:

```
Driving the real streamSimpleAzureOpenAIResponses provider path; capturing the outbound HTTP request on a loopback server.

PASS  mixed-case request resolves to the mapped deployment (was Azure 404 before the fix)
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o"
      request model.id="GPT-4o"  ->  outgoing request body.model="deployment-gpt-4o"  (expected "deployment-gpt-4o")
PASS  exact-case mapping is preserved on the wire (no regression)
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="GPT-4o=prod-a,gpt-4o=prod-b"
      request model.id="GPT-4o"  ->  outgoing request body.model="prod-a"  (expected "prod-a")
PASS  unmapped model id falls back to the raw id on the wire
      AZURE_OPENAI_DEPLOYMENT_NAME_MAP="gpt-4o=deployment-gpt-4o"
      request model.id="gpt-5"  ->  outgoing request body.model="gpt-5"  (expected "gpt-5")

ALL PROVIDER-PATH CHECKS PASSED
```

This is codified as a committed integration test
(`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-openai-responses.deployment-map.test.ts`) so the
provider path stays covered in CI.

### Focused tests

`packages/ai/src/providers/azure-deployment-map.test.ts` (7) plus the provider-path
test (2) — 9 passed:

```
 ✓ preserves equals signs inside deployment names
 ✓ falls back to the model id when the map has no usable entry
```

target.title: Rescue: add watchdog core service and cron engine
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: OpenClaw had no built-in isolated rescue watchdog that could detect an unhealthy managed gateway profile and repair it without going through the failing primary session.
- Why it matters: the larger rescue-watchdog feature is hard to review as one PR; this split lands the core runtime/service layer first so maintainers can review the actual watchdog mechanism without onboarding/UI noise.
- What changed: adds daemon/service hardening needed by the watchdog, introduces a new isolated `rescueWatchdog` cron payload + runner, and wires the gateway cron service to execute that watchdog job against a monitored profile.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no onboarding wizard flow, no CLI `openclaw onboard --rescue-watchdog` UX, and no docs changes in this PR.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
